record.paper_title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
record.original_question: Does every non-totally disconnected topological group have a quotient group that is non-trivial and separable?

evidence.quote: Does every non-totally disconnected topological group have a quotient group which is a non-trivial separable topological group?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological group is a group $G$ endowed with a topology such that the multiplication map $G\times G\to G$ and the inversion map $G\to G$ are continuous. A topological group $G$ is called totally disconnected if the connected component of its identity element consists of the identity alone. A topological space is called separable if it contains a countable dense subset. By a quotient group of $G$ we mean the topological group $G/N$, equipped with the quotient topology, for some closed normal subgroup $N$ of $G$; such a quotient is non-trivial if $G/N$ has more than one element.

Determine whether the following statement is true: for every topological group $G$ that is not totally disconnected, there exists a closed normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ such that the quotient topological group $G/N$ is non-trivial and separable.
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been resolved in the negative. Work on the separable quotient problem for topological groups establishes that there exist non-totally disconnected topological groups with no non-trivial separable quotient. Positive answers are nevertheless obtained for many important classes (compact groups, locally compact abelian groups, σ-compact locally compact groups, abelian pro-Lie groups, σ-compact pro-Lie groups, pseudocompact groups).

status_evidence.title: The Separable Quotient Problem for Topological Groups (arXiv:1707.09546)
status_evidence.snippet: All four questions are answered here in the negative... positive answers are proved for important classes including compact groups, locally compact abelian groups, σ-compact locally compact groups, abelian pro-Lie groups, σ-compact pro-Lie groups, pseudocompact groups.
status_evidence.claim: The general question of whether every non-totally disconnected topological group has a non-trivial separable quotient is answered negatively.

status_evidence.title: The separable quotient problem for topological groups, Israel J. Math.
status_evidence.snippet: Published study of the separable quotient problem for topological groups, providing negative answers in general and positive answers for many classes.
status_evidence.claim: The problem has been published with a negative resolution in general.
